mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 2% for three consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a rise in the Houston housing sales index (HOUST) signals a consumption contraction offset by a housing demand rebound, resulting in flat to slightly positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST > previous 6-month average
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer and business spending, which in turn depresses corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% while the unemployment rate is below 4% signals a supply-side shock in an otherwise tight labor market, which raises input costs and reduces profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
regime_hint: tight labor market with supply shock
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.3%) in at least 50% of triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid acceleration in payroll employment growth above 300k new jobs per month for three consecutive months signals a strong labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly change > 300000 for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly decline in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing sales (HOUST) by more than 1% signals a broad-based weakening in demand, which reduces corporate revenue and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 monthly change < -1.0% AND HOUST monthly change < -1.0%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.6%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month increase in the federal funds rate of more than 0.75 percentage points signals an aggressive tightening stance, which immediately raises risk-free rates and equity discount rates, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.4%) in at least 50% of triggered events.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in the industrial production index (INDPRO) above 0.8% for four consecutive months signals a robust supply-side expansion, which boosts corporate capacity and earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days in any macro regime.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered months.
